workflow_instructions.mode_overview: This mode gives an existing BAW process app a React + Carbon UI without touching its logic. You analyze each legacy coach and design a better screen as a coach spec. For every client-side human service, the baw-dev-tools MCP server adds a copy named "(Modernized)" whose coaches are layouts of Modernizer Widgets (the MDW toolkit: Header, fields, Error Summary, Button) inside UI Toolkit panels and tabs, styled by the app's theme file. Authors can open these coaches in Coach Designer and drag, drop and rearrange the widgets. A coach whose spec names a "screen" shows a React screen you wrote for it instead, as one block. The original buttons stay in each coach, hidden, and the widgets or your screen press them, so the coach flow and its scripts run unchanged. The legacy services stay next to the copies.

step.details: When the switch reason names an app just built, use it: its acronym, snapshot, .twx, coach spec and theme file. Do not ask for the acronym, do not call export_app, and skip the legacy test_service, since the app was just tested. Run inspect_coaches on the .twx only when the coach spec is missing. When the App Builder rebuilt an app you had already planned or modernized, run inspect_coaches on the new .twx with previous set to the coach spec you edited before: it carries your edits (theme, labels, types, titles) over, and reports the ones the app changed since or that found nothing to go to. Keep the theme file unless the user asked for another look. Then continue with "Improve the spec" in the analyze phase.

Ask for the process app acronym when it is not given; list_apps and list_snapshots help. Modernized copies install as a new snapshot of the source app. When you did not create that app in this task, say so at the design stop and install only after the user approves.

steps.step: export_app, inspect_coaches; test_service on the legacy service to see the screens as users do today
Improve the spec: human labels, section titles, required fields, patterns, examples, read-only review coaches
Set the spec's "theme" to the app's theme file; without one, ask the user to describe the look and write work/NAME.theme.json with the app-theme skill

When a coach needs a field no Modernizer Widget gives (for example a Yes/No Toggle for a Boolean), plan a new widget: what single value it saves, its options, and which fields use it. Never plan a change to an existing widget

Keep the groups inspect_coaches read back; propose its groupCandidates, or the groups the user named, as reusable groups (coach-groups skill). A group's fields are listed once, in the spec's "groups": edit a group's field there, not in the coaches that place it

Check the request against what the coach spec can change. Buttons (a new Cancel, a renamed Submit), fields, steps, a workflow or an approval live in the app spec: the Modernizer cannot add or rename them. When the request needs one, put it first in the plan as an App Builder change, and on approval switch to BAW App Builder before building anything here, so the app is rebuilt once and modernized once

STOP unless told to continue: show what is wrong with the legacy screens, your design for each coach, the theme file, the spec changes, the groups and where each is placed, the new widgets (what each saves, its options, the fields that use it), and the App Builder changes the request needs first

phase.name: build
phase.description: The coach-modernize skill, and the react-coach-screen skill for hand-written screens

steps.step: Pick the toolkit: the newest snapshot list_snapshots("MDW") shows that has its work/MDW-SNAPSHOT.twx. When there is none, or the widgets changed since, build_widget_toolkit("modernizer") with a new snapshot and install_app it. When the plan adds a widget, follow the modernizer-widget skill, then always build a new snapshot and install it

Coaches are built from Modernizer Widgets by default. Only when the user asks for a screen designed for a coach, or the design needs more than the widgets give (a layout, component or behaviour the spec cannot express), write a screen in coach-ui/src/screens/: when the carbon-mcp tools are available, code_search the Carbon components and docs_search the patterns first, and code_audit the screen after (react-coach-screen skill). Set "screen" on that coach, build_screens

modernize_app with a new snapshot and toolkit_snapshot. When it returns changedInBaw, ask per group whether to keep BAW's version or replace it, and modernize_app again with replace_groups for the ones to replace. Then install_app
test_service for every modernized service with fill; look at the screenshots, fix and repeat until right
Report each service with its result, the screens written, the new widgets (files and the fields using them) with the MDW snapshot, and before / after screenshots

phase.name: hand_off
phase.description: When the user asks for a new app, or for a change to what an app collects: switch to BAW App Builder

steps.step: A new app from a requirement or screenshots, or new or removed fields, steps, a workflow or an approval, changes the app spec, not the screens. Call switch_mode with mode_id "baw-app-builder" without asking: the user's request is the go-ahead. Never in your first reply of a task (see .bob/rules/baw-mode-routing.md): when the request is the task's first message, call list_files on work/ first
In the reason, give the app name, acronym, installed snapshots, the app spec and theme file when you know them, and repeat what the user asked for
Labels, help text, grouping, validation, the look and screen behaviour stay here: they live in the coach spec, the theme file and the React screens

A change to what an existing Modernizer Widget shows or does, for every app that uses it, is a code change in coach-ui/: switch to agent mode with the widget and the change in the reason. Adding a new widget stays here

completion_criteria.criterion: Every service marked "modernize": true has its "(Modernized)" copy installed, styled by the theme file
test_service reports "ok": true for every copy, and you have looked at the screenshots
The report lists the services, the snapshot, the MDW toolkit snapshot, the new widgets (if any), the screens written (if any), screenshot folders, and what the spec kept native or dropped
